title: Compass Canonical Structural Elements — Developmental Exit Criteria
principle: These criteria do NOT judge writing quality. They determine whether a learner has done enough developmental work on a structural element to proceed to the next authentic cognitive operation. Compass asks: 'Can this element now support the next developmental operation?' YES -> stop teaching this element, proceed. NO -> continue instruction. The standard is developmental sufficiency, not maximal quality.

canonical_explanations.thesis: A thesis tells your reader the main idea your essay is trying to establish.
canonical_explanations.controlling_idea: A controlling idea tells your reader the main point this paragraph is making.
canonical_explanations.definition: A definition helps your reader understand what a key idea means before you build other ideas on it.
canonical_explanations.evidence: Evidence gives your reader reasons to believe a claim.
canonical_explanations.explanation: Explanation shows your reader how the evidence supports the claim.
canonical_explanations.transition: A transition helps readers understand how one idea connects to the next.
canonical_explanations.synthesis: Synthesis shows your reader how several ideas fit together into a larger point.
canonical_explanations.example: An example gives your reader a concrete case that makes an abstract idea clearer.
canonical_explanations.paragraph_purpose: Each paragraph should do one clear job that helps the whole essay.
canonical_explanations.communicative_purpose: Your purpose is what you want your reader to understand or believe by the end.
canonical_explanations.overall_organization: Organization is the order that lets your reader follow your ideas from start to finish.
canonical_explanations.introduction: An introduction prepares your reader for what the essay will be about and why it matters.
canonical_explanations.reader_guidance: Reader guidance keeps your reader clear about who and what you are talking about.
canonical_explanations.closure: A conclusion gives your reader a sense that the writing has arrived at a resting point.
canonical_explanations.sentence_purpose: Each sentence should do one clear job in the paragraph.
canonical_explanations.sentence_relationships: Sentences should connect so your reader sees why each one follows the last.

elements.name: Communicative Purpose
elements.purpose: Identify what the writer is trying to accomplish.
elements.exit_criterion: Can the remainder of the composition be organized around a reasonably clear communicative purpose?

elements.name: Overall Organization
elements.purpose: Provide a coherent progression toward the communicative purpose.
elements.cognitive_operation: Organize major ideas into an understandable whole.
elements.exit_criterion: Can the reader reasonably follow the intended progression of ideas?

elements.name: Introduction
elements.purpose: Prepare the reader for the composition.
elements.exit_criterion: Can the reader understand what this composition will be about and why it matters?

elements.name: Paragraph Purpose
elements.purpose: Establish the contribution this paragraph makes to the whole composition.
elements.cognitive_operation: Determine what work this paragraph performs.
elements.exit_criterion: Can the paragraph be understood as accomplishing one identifiable purpose?

elements.name: Controlling Idea (Paragraph Thesis)
elements.cognitive_operation: Express the central idea that governs the paragraph.
elements.exit_criterion: Can the remaining sentences reasonably develop this idea?

elements.name: Definition
elements.purpose: Enable the reader to understand an important concept.
elements.exit_criterion: Can the concept now be used in subsequent explanation without confusing the reader?

elements.name: Explanation
elements.purpose: Help the reader understand why or how.
elements.exit_criterion: Can the reader understand the intended relationship among the ideas?

elements.name: Evidence
elements.cognitive_operation: Connect claims to observations, examples, or sources.
elements.exit_criterion: Can the claim now be reasonably accepted or considered by the reader?

elements.name: Example
elements.exit_criterion: Does the example genuinely help the reader understand the idea?

elements.name: Transition
elements.purpose: Help readers understand relationships between ideas.
elements.exit_criterion: Can the reader understand why the next idea follows from the previous one?

elements.name: Reader Guidance
elements.exit_criterion: Can the reader easily follow who, what, and which idea is being discussed?

elements.name: Synthesis
elements.purpose: Show how multiple ideas work together.
elements.exit_criterion: Can the reader understand the larger meaning created by combining the ideas?

elements.name: Closure
elements.exit_criterion: Can the reader recognize that this unit of writing has reached a natural stopping point?

elements.name: Sentence Purpose
elements.purpose: Ensure each sentence performs a recognizable function.
elements.exit_criterion: Does this sentence perform an identifiable function within the paragraph?

elements.name: Sentence Relationships
elements.cognitive_operation: Relate each sentence to surrounding sentences.
elements.exit_criterion: Can the reader understand why each sentence belongs where it is?

elements.name: Thesis (Whole-Essay Controlling Idea)
elements.purpose: State the single central idea the whole essay exists to establish.
elements.cognitive_operation: Commit to one arguable, supportable central claim that answers the task.
elements.exit_criterion: Can every part of the essay be organized around this one central claim, and could a thoughtful reader restate it?
failure_modes: fact or question instead of a position
claim the body does not develop

general_constitutional_rule: Compass should never continue teaching a structural element merely because additional improvement is theoretically possible. Instruction ends when the current element can adequately support the learner's next authentic cognitive operation. The objective function is developmental progress, not local perfection.
